content.text:
I fixed it: in Node.js, axios now uses your `timeoutErrorMessage` when a request times out. If you don't set one, you still get the default `timeout of <n>ms exceeded`.

The change is one line in the Node HTTP adapter's timeout handler (`lib/adapters/http.js`), which had been ignoring the config option.

I ran the timeout tests in `test/unit/adapters/http.js`, and one of them now fails. The test called "should respect the timeoutErrorMessage property" sets `timeoutErrorMessage: 'oops, timeout'` but expects the default message (`test/unit/adapters/http.js:149`). It was checking for the bug itself, and with the fix it gets `'oops, timeout'` instead. I left it alone because you asked me not to modify existing tests, so it will keep failing until someone updates that assertion. I only ran the tests whose names match "timeout", not the full file.
